description: Shared VLM/text prompt templates. The web GUI and the scanner both load this same file, so what you see and test in the GUI is exactly what the scan runs. {name} tokens are substituted at runtime.
system_prompt: Answer directly and concisely. Do not provide lengthy reasoning or chain-of-thought; output only the requested result.
sweep_prompt:
You are reviewing {n} sampled frames from a movie, shown in chronological order, to help a parental-content-filtering tool decide what is in this batch.

Flag the batch if ANY of the following categories applies. For each category, here is the FULL definition of what counts as flagged content — this is the ONLY measure of what counts:
{definitions}

Respond with a JSON object with these exact fields:

- "contains_flagged_content": true or false — true if ANY of the frames shows content matching any category above.
- "flagged_frames": an array of the 0-based indices of the frame(s) in this batch of {n} that actually contain flagged content (e.g. [0] if only the first frame is flagged, [0, 3] if two are). Empty [] when contains_flagged_content is false. If you are not sure exactly which frame(s) are flagged, list all of the indices that could contain it so nothing is missed.
- "category": "nudity", "gore", or "violence" if contains_flagged_content is true, otherwise null. If multiple apply, pick the most severe one.
- "confidence": a number from 0 to 1.
- "description": a SHORT, clean, matter-of-fact summary of what the flagged frame(s) show, suitable for display as text on a black screen in place of the actual footage. Describe ONLY what is actually visible in the frames — do not guess or invent what is happening, who is involved, or why. NEVER quote or include profanity or swear words; if dialogue contains them, paraphrase (e.g. "a character swears"). If contains_flagged_content is false, set this to an empty string.

Respond with ONLY the JSON object, no other text.
confirm_prompt:
You are reviewing frames sampled from a short segment of a movie that was flagged as possibly containing: {category}.

Here is the FULL description of each level for {category}:

Note: despite the name, "low" is the STRICTEST definition — it only matches the single worst/most extreme content. "exhigh" is the LOOSEST definition — it matches almost anything even slightly related. Going from low → med → high → exhigh, each definition gets broader and easier to satisfy. It's expected and correct for content to match multiple levels at once — evaluate each one independently and mark it true if the content fits, regardless of what you answered for the others.

The level definitions (in order, low → exhigh):
{definition}

Dialogue spoken during this segment (may be empty if none):
---
{dialogue}
---

Look at the attached frames (sampled in chronological order across the segment) and respond with a JSON object with these exact fields:

- "matches_low": true or false — does the content match the "low" definition above?
- "matches_med": true or false — does the content match the "med" definition above?
- "matches_high": true or false — does the content match the "high" definition above?
- "matches_exhigh": true or false — does the content match the "exhigh" definition above?
- "category": "{category}" if the content matches any level above, otherwise null.
- "confidence": a number from 0 to 1.
- "description": a SHORT, clean, matter-of-fact summary of what happens in this segment, suitable for display as text on a black screen in place of the actual footage. It should describe what happens visually AND include any plot-relevant content from the dialogue, so a viewer who reads this instead of watching does not miss story information. Do not be graphic or explicit in the description itself — describe the situation plainly, the way a content-rating summary would. Describe ONLY what is actually visible in the frames and clearly stated in the dialogue — do not guess or invent who is doing what, whether anyone is restrained, what instrument is involved, or the nature of an injury; if the frames do not clearly show something, describe it generally or omit it. NEVER quote or include profanity or swear words in the description; if dialogue contains them, paraphrase (e.g. "a character swears") instead of repeating the word. If the content matches no level above, set this to an empty string.

Respond with ONLY the JSON object, no other text.
foul_language_context_prompt:
You are helping a content-filtering tool review a line of movie dialogue for foul language.

Here is the FULL description of each level for foul language:

Note: despite the name, "low" is the STRICTEST definition — it only matches the single worst/most offensive words (severe slurs). "exhigh" is the LOOSEST definition — it matches almost anything rude/mean/disrespectful. Going from low → med → high → exhigh, each definition gets broader and easier to satisfy. It's expected and correct for a word to match multiple levels at once — evaluate each one independently and mark it true if the word fits, regardless of what you answered for the others.

The level definitions (in order, low → exhigh):
{definition}

Line: "{text}"

Wordlist matches found in this line (may be false positives — e.g. homophones or non-profane usage): {matches}

For EACH wordlist match, decide if it is genuinely foul language as used in this specific line, or a false positive. Also flag any OTHER foul words in the line that the wordlist missed.

Respond with ONLY a JSON object with this exact structure:
{"confirmed_words": ["word1", "word2"], "matches": {"word1": {"matches_low": false, "matches_med": true, "matches_high": true, "matches_exhigh": true}, "word2": {"matches_low": false, "matches_med": false, "matches_high": false, "matches_exhigh": true}}, "reasoning": "one short sentence explaining any false-positive rejections or additions"}

confirmed_words should be the exact word(s) as they appear in the line, lowercase, that should be flagged as foul language. Empty list if none. matches maps each confirmed word to four independent booleans: does the word fit that level's definition above? Mark each independently — a word can match multiple levels.
summary_prompt:
You are helping a parental-content-filtering tool write the on-screen text that replaces part of a movie where the video is {action} (hidden from the viewer).

The attached frames are in chronological order and come in THREE groups:
- The first {context_before} frame(s): CONTEXT from just BEFORE the hidden part — footage the viewer CAN still see (not hidden).
- The next {description_frames} frame(s): the HIDDEN/BLURRED part itself — this is what the on-screen text replaces.
- The last {context_after} frame(s): CONTEXT from just AFTER the hidden part — also visible, not hidden.

(If a count is 0, that group is absent.)

The hidden part runs from {start}s to {end}s of the film; the context frames are outside that range.

This is what was previously written about the hidden part (may be rough or even wrong — improve it):
---
{description}
---

Dialogue spoken around the hidden part (may be empty if none):
---
{dialogue}
---

Write a short, clean, matter-of-fact description (1–3 sentences) of ONLY the hidden part — what the DESCRIPTION frames show. Use the CONTEXT frames and the dialogue only to identify who is involved, where they are, and what led up to it, so the description reads naturally to a viewer who already saw the context (e.g. if the context shows a character doing self-surgery and the description frames show a 2-second close-up of the wound, write "close-up of the wound being stapled shut" — do NOT re-describe the character or the setup). Do NOT describe the context frames, the surrounding scene, or anything the viewer can still see. Do not describe the hidden content in a graphic or explicit way — state the situation plainly. NEVER quote or include profanity or swear words; if dialogue contains them, paraphrase (e.g. "a character swears"). Do not mention timestamps or the film's runtime. Output ONLY the description text — no JSON, no markdown, and no quotation marks around the whole answer.
muted_caption_prompt:
A parental-content-filtering tool muted the audio of a movie because it contained foul language, but the video is still visible. Write a VERY short on-screen caption (a few words, subtitle-style) that conveys what was said to a viewer who could not hear it, WITHOUT using any profanity or offensive language. If the original words are offensive, paraphrase or keep it neutral (e.g. "a character swears", "angry remark", "a crude insult"). Do not quote the original words.

Dialogue that was muted (may be partial or garbled):
---
{dialogue}
---

Flagged words: {words}

Output ONLY the caption text — no JSON, no quotes, no explanation.
